sentences: The degree of idealization also predicts the degree of demonization for me.
I don’t mean this as a clinical diagnosis, but I use it almost diagnostically in my own life.
If a woman says, “You’re such a great guy.
Of course you have flaws like anyone, but I love you,” that sounds healthy.
If she says, “You’re perfect, I can’t find any flaw,” I’m already running.
When the BPD splitting happens, that worship can turn into hatred, first in private and then in front of everybody.
She rewrites our whole history until every flaw of mine looks like evidence I was faking it the whole time.
Sometimes the woman who thought I was perfect later accuses me of thinking I’m perfect.
